why: Single source of truth for main's required status-check contexts. Two things read it: scripts/ci/assert-repo-policy.sh (asserts GitHub's live branch protection + ruleset carry exactly these) and scripts/ci/verify-release-pr-checks.mjs (asserts a release PR's head commit is actually going to report them). Keeping the list in one file is the F-1135 lesson applied to CI contexts: a second hand-maintained copy goes stale while still looking like something is watching.
note: These are job NAMES as GitHub renders them on a commit's check-runs: `typecheck-test` (ci.yml), `gitleaks + trufflehog` (secret-scan.yml), `dependency review` (dependency-review.yml). Renaming a job renames its context and silently drops the required check — change this file in the same PR.
